title: Trombone Emoji (🪊): Codepoint, Meaning & the Sad-Trombone Use
meta_description: The trombone emoji 🪊 (U+1FA8A): its Unicode 17.0 codepoint, how to type it, and why the slide is the detail that made a separate emoji necessary.
hero_tagline: The slide trombone 🪊 with its codepoint, its input routes, the brass and woodwind it sits beside, and the one comic cue it gets typed for most. Tap the trombone to copy it; the trumpet below is the glyph it kept getting substituted for.
intro: 🪊 TROMBONE (U+1FA8A) joined Unicode in version 17.0 and landed on most phones with iOS 26.4 in March 2026. The instrument shelf already held a trumpet, and the argument for a second brass glyph was the slide: a trombone changes pitch by moving a tube rather than pressing valves, which is both what a player sees and what the descending "womp womp" cue depends on. That cue is why this emoji gets typed far more often than any orchestral use would predict.
